transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-20
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 mins (approx)
Attendees: Michael Chen, Priya Nair, Jordan Li (Redwood); Liam O'Connor, Maya Ruiz, Daniel Park, Sara Goldman (TritonBridge)
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai export

Summary:
Quick technical walkthrough of Redwood SDK (Python + TypeScript) quickstart, auth patterns (API key vs. VPC private deploy), and initial perf/cost expectations. Agreed on bench test plan and delivered action items for sandbox access and security scoping.

Topics covered:
- SDK quickstart (py/ts) and env vars
- Auth options: hosted API key, dedicated, private VPC + KMS
- Console walkthrough: routes, models, cost breakdowns
- Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching + quantization
- Bench plan: 3 scenarios, latency/cost targets

Shared artifacts:
- Quickstart repo (link): https://github.com/redwood-inference/tritonbridge-quickstart
- Slide deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/tritonbridge-quickstart (first pass)
- Bench template (sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/bench-template

Transcript body:
[00:00] Michael (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to under an hour. I'm Michael, AE, with Priya our SE and Jordan from DevRel. Quick intro from you folks?
[00:12] Liam (TritonBridge): Hey yeah Liam here, lead eng, glad to sync.
[00:15] Maya (TritonBridge): Maya, ops, I'll be handling infra and networking.
[00:18] Daniel (TritonBridge): Daniel, CTO, quick overview and timelines from our side.
[00:22] Sara (TritonBridge): Sara, security. We'll need SOC2 arte — uh, artifacts and a short questionnaire.
[00:28] Michael: Great. Agenda: quick SDK setup (py/ts), auth pattern choices, a console tour, then bench plan and next steps. Priya will lead the deep dive.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll share my screen — so starting with a tiny python example, it's basically pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env, then a simple generation call.
[00:50] Priya: Code snippet: from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = c.generate(model='redwood-3b', prompt='Summarize...') — you can see it's synchronous by default, but we also recommend streaming for low latency.
[01:10] Liam: Quick q — we currently use Anthropic for some customer-facing flows, main concerns are latency spikes during peak. How do you handle that?
[01:18] Priya: Good question. We do continuous batching in the runtime and prefix KV caching — reduces per token compute. If you need dedicated throughput, Redwood Dedicated gives predictable p99s, but hosted with autoscaling is often enough if you tune batching and caching.
[01:34] Maya: When you say K-V, is that key-value cache or KMS?
[01:37] Priya: KL — K-V cache, sorry, like the KV cache in the LLM context; not KMS. KMS is for keys, we'll cover that in the security section.
[01:45] Jordan (Redwood DevRel): Also note: Optimize suggests batching window sizes based on your seq length distribution — we'll show you the console recommendations.
[01:55] Daniel: For auth, we need SAML + KMS + on-prem options. Can you do a private deployment?
[02:02] Michael: Yes. Three patterns: hosted (API keys + roles), Dedicated/reserved pools for throughput and isolation, and Private (VPC or on-prem) with customer-managed control plane. For KMS we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM via our private packages.
[02:21] Sara: We need the SOC2 cert and network diagram to present to legal.
[02:24] Michael: We'll attach SOC2 and the VPC peering diagram. Action item noted.
[02:30] Priya: Back to SDK — switching to TypeScript, the install is @redwood/sdk, then set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY. Example: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); client.chat.create(...).
[02:47] [crosstalk]
[02:50] Priya: Sorry, small audio glitch — continuing. For streaming from Node, we expose an async iterator that yields tokens, which is handy for progressive rendering in the UI.
[03:05] Liam: Any gotchas on CORS or browser usage?
[03:08] Jordan: We don't recommend embedding API keys in browsers. Typical pattern: short-lived tokens via your backend or use our session tokens. We can show you the token rotation pattern.
[03:20] Maya: On network, if we go private, do we need to open ports to your control plane?
[03:24] Priya: For Private deployments, control plane is customer managed inside your VPC; for hosted, you only need outbound to our regional endpoints. We'll share the exact CIDR ranges and peering steps.
[03:40] Daniel: Can we pin a model version for rollouts? We want canary releases, A/B.
[03:44] Priya: Yes, model pinning and rollout policies are first class. Console supports canary and automatic fallbacks.
[03:50] Michael: Let's jump to the console — Priya, can you click through the route and model dashboards?
[03:54] Priya: Showing the console now — top left is project selector, then routes. Each route has token cost breakdown and latency histograms. Here you can set per-route batching, cache TTLs, and a default quantization profile.
[04:18] [00:04:18] Priya: Note the trace view — if an eval regresses, you can link to prompt sets and rollback.
[04:30] Liam: On cost, what's the rough per-1k-token delta vs Anthropic? Ballpark.
[04:35] Michael: Ballpark depends on model and quantization; we're generally 10-40% lower for similar quality when you use our Optimize recommendations. We'll provide a cost comparison spreadsheet.
[04:50] Maya: About the quickstart repo — will it include a docker compose for local sim?
[04:55] Jordan: Yes, repo includes a sandbox docker-compose that runs a stubbed local server, and examples in both Python and TS. Link again: github.com/redwood-inference/tritonbridge-quickstart.
[05:08] [05:08] Priya: Now, perf bench plan — we recommend three scenarios: short chat (avg 40 tokens), long generation (avg 600 tokens), and streaming-rich interactive. We'll run p50/p90/p99, and tokens-per-dollar.
[05:25] Daniel: Targets: p90 < 350ms for short chat, cost under $0.009 per 1k tokens for baseline — ballpark.
[05:32] Priya: Sounds reasonable. We'll tailor the model choice — redwood-3b or 7b quantized options.
[05:40] Liam: Anything special for TypeScript types?
[05:44] Jordan: We include full d.ts and example types. The SDK auto-generates types from the model schema, but the initial quickstart uses typed wrappers.
[05:55] Sara: Security question — do you store prompts? Retention settings?
[05:59] Michael: By default we retain data for 30 days for debugging, but you can opt-out and set retention to zero. Dedicated and Private give you full control over logs and audit retention. We'll send the data retention policy.
[06:10] Maya: KMS integration — if we want keys in our HSM, is that supported?
[06:13] Priya: Yes, either via customer KMS in Private or bring-your-own-HSM for Private on-prem. For hosted, we use envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS where possible.
[06:25] [06:25] Liam: Okay good. Let's talk bench details — Priya, what do you need from our side to run the three scenarios?
[06:29] Priya: The typical inputs: sample prompts per scenario (you can reuse anonymized traffic), expected concurrency (rps), and sequence length distribution. Maya, can you share current traffic profiles?
[06:40] Maya: We'll extract that, yes. We'll need instructions on anonymization.
[06:44] Priya: We'll provide a small script and an ingestion template.
[06:48] Jordan: Also, we'll include an example CI job that runs the bench and uploads results to the bench sheet.
[06:53] [06:53] Michael: On the commercial side, quick note — Dedicated pricing has a minimum commit; we'll surface options in the deck.
[07:00] Daniel: For pilot, we'll likely start hosted to iterate fast, then switch to Dedicated if p99s or throughput need it.
[07:06] Michael: That's a common pattern.
[07:10] [07:10] Priya: Quick live code demo: I'm opening the python quickstart — env var REDWOOD_API_KEY set to sandbox key. Running the sample script... output shows streaming tokens, you can see latency ~120ms for token bursts in my demo env.
[07:32] Michael: Note that's a small demo env, actual will differ.
[07:36] Liam: Do you have sample latency numbers for the 7b quantized model?
[07:40] Priya: Typical p50 around 130-200ms for short responses when quantized on latest infra, p90 depends on concurrency. We'll run that in the bench.
[07:50] [07:50] Maya: Regarding CI secrets, how do you recommend rotating keys?
[07:54] Jordan: Use short-lived tokens via our token exchange endpoint — we have an example GitHub Actions step that rotates tokens and stores only ephemeral creds.
[08:03] Priya: Also for on-prem there's an operator you can deploy that uses your internal vault.
[08:09] Sara: Want to flag that legal will ask about subprocessor list and backup/DR.
[08:13] Michael: We'll include subprocessors doc and backup RTO/RPO info.
[08:19] [08:19] Liam: One hiccup — we use a custom NLU that expects consistent output shapes. How do you enforce structured outputs?
[08:24] Priya: We recommend function-calling style responses or schema-guided generation. Our SDK has a structured output helper that validates JSON schema and returns parse errors if the model deviates.
[08:36] Daniel: Great. Can we run a small integration test with our NLU in the bench?
[08:40] Priya: Yes, include that as a scenario; we'll execute end-to-end.
[08:43] [08:43] Michael: Let's capture next steps...
[08:45] Michael: Action items recap: Michael share repo and deck (due 8/22). Priya to set up bench harness (due 8/27). Maya to share VPC details (due 8/25). Sara to send security questionnaire (due 8/24). We'll schedule follow-up for 8/27 or 8/28 to review bench results.
[08:59] Liam: Sounds good. Couple of misc Qs — will the console show per-route token attribution to individual users?
[09:05] Priya: Yes, you can tag tokens by request metadata and get user-level cost breakdowns.
[09:12] Maya: For rollout, can we auto-fallback to smaller models on congestion?
[09:15] Priya: Yes, you can define routing policies: latency-first or cost-first. We have automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
[09:23] Daniel: Any pitfalls if we try to start with private right away?
[09:26] Michael: Private is doable but has longer lead time due to network & compliance setup; pilot on hosted is faster.
[09:32] [09:32] Jordan: Quick note: the SDK contains a sample tracer middleware for OpenTelemetry that plugs into your existing tracing.
[09:40] Sara: That helps for audit.
[09:43] Michael: Okay, final questions?
[09:45] [09:45] Liam: None from me.
[09:46] Maya: Nope.
[09:47] Daniel: All set.
[09:48] Michael: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send notes and the links after this call.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: There are occasional mis-hearings (K-V cash typed as K-V cash in a couple spots in live audio). Some speaker labels may shift while people were on mute.
